page.overview:
What is Dhumin?

Dhumin is a fictional entity created by American author Beecher Smith for his short Cthulhu Mythos story "The Burrower From the Bluff."

Dhumin is hinted at by Chief Russell Two Bears as being a Great Old One, or perhaps a species of colossal worm unknown to modern science (see "Behind the Mythos," below). (: "The Burrower From the Bluff")

One description given by Chief Two Bears is of Native American legends telling of Dhumin being "the most terrible" of the Uktena, "a great snake of the underworld" with "antlers like a deer and wings like an eagle." These creatures are said to inhabit "the deep waters, high places, and caverns beneath the earth … bor[ing] like the earthworm, and travel[ling] freely between the land of the living… and of the dead." (: "The Burrower From the Bluff")

The entity has a dislike of the sun and light in general, although it is only stated to be truly afraid of fire. (: "The Burrower From the Bluff")
